{{nihongo|'''Ajika Shrine'''|阿遅加神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Ajika Shrine''' (あぢかじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Hashima, Gifu|Q819595|qid=Q819595}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gifu|af|Gifu-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gifu|ar|غيفو (محافظة)|arz|جيفو (محافظه)|az|Gifu prefekturası|azb|قیفو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gifu|be|Гіфу (прэфектура)|bg|Гифу|bn|গিফু প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gifu|cdo|Gifu-gâing|ce|Гифу (префектура)|ceb|Gifu-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گیفو|cs|Prefektura Gifu|cy|Gifu (talaith)|da|Gifu-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gifu|eo|Gubernio Gifu|es|Prefectura de Gifu|et|Gifu prefektuur|eu|Gifu (prefektura)|fa|استان گیفو|fi|Gifun prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gifu|frr|Gifu (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gifu|gl|Prefectura de Gifu|hak|Gifu-yen|he|גיפו (מחוז)|hr|Gifu (prefektura)|hu|Gifu prefektúra|hy|Գիֆու (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gifu|ilo|Prepektura ti Gifu|it|Prefettura di Gifu|ja|岐阜県|jv|Préfèktur Gifu|ka|გიფუს პრეფექტურა|kn|ಗಿಫು (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|기후현|lt|Gifu prefektūra|lv|Gifu prefektūra|mk|Гифу (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯤꯐꯨ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गिफू प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gifu|ne|गिफु|nl|Gifu (prefectuur)|no|Gifu (prefektur)|nov|Gifu Prefekture|os|Гифу (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gifu|pl|Prefektura Gifu|pnb|ضلع گیفو|pt|Gifu|ro|Prefectura Gifu|ru|Гифу (префектура)|se|Gifu prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gifu|simple|Gifu Prefecture|sk|Gifu (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гифу|su|Préféktur Gifu|sv|Gifu prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gifu|tg|Префектураи Гифу|th|จังหวัดกิฟุ|tl|Prepektura ng Gifu|tr|Gifu (prefektörlük)|tt|Гифу (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґіфу|ur|گیفو پریفیکچر|vi|Gifu|war|Gifu (prefektura)|wuu|岐阜县|zh|岐阜县|zh_classical|岐阜縣|zh_min_nan|Gihu-koān|zh_yue|岐阜縣|qid=Q131277}}. It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}} {{ill|Haguri District|Q1032507|qid=Q1032507}}).

=== Overview ===
* After completing his eastern expedition and arriving in {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}} headed for {{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}} to defeat the deity of {{ill|Mount Ibuki|Q2624360|qid=Q2624360}}. Learning of a sacred spring near the river marking the border between Owari and Mino (corresponding to the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}} before {{ill|1586|Q6739|qid=Q6739}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 14); today’s {{ill|Sakai River (Gifu)|Q4330698|qid=Q4330698|lt=Sakai River}}), Yamato Takeru drank from the spring and rested for a time. The place where this sacred spring existed is said to be the site of Ajika Shrine.
* After Yamato Takeru died on his way back to {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}}, his son Wak Takehiko no Ō visited this place and built a shrine to enshrine Yamato Takeru, which is said to be the origin of the shrine.
* In {{ill|1586|Q6739|qid=Q6739}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 14), the Kiso River drastically changed its course due to a major flood. The border between Owari and Mino was shifted to the new course of the Kiso River, and the location of Ajika Shrine was changed from Haguri District, Owari Province, to {{ill|Haguri district|Q11610214|qid=Q11610214}}, Mino Province.
* During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called “Waka no Miya,” “Hachiman Shrine,” and “Yatsurugi Daimyōjin.” In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the name was restored to Ajika Shrine.
* In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6), it was designated a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru no Mikoto}}
** There is also a theory that the enshrined deity is Mononobe no Ajiko no Muraji (the younger brother of {{ill|Mononobe no Arakabi|Q1114837|qid=Q1114837}}, the {{ill|Ōmuraji|Q4328807|qid=Q4328807|lt=Ōmuraji}} who subdued the {{ill|Iwai Rebellion|Q3138004|qid=Q3138004}}).

=== Location ===
* 1088-2 Nao-michi, Ashika-chō, Hashima City, Gifu Prefecture

=== Transportation ===
{{commonscat|Ajika-jinja}}
* Get off at the “Sakai” bus stop on the {{ill|Hashima City Community Bus|Q11610099|qid=Q11610099}} Blue Bus line; 3-minute walk.
* About a 20-minute walk from {{ill|Minami-Juku Station|Q11407722|qid=Q11407722}} on the {{ill|Meitetsu Takehana Line|Q901442|qid=Q901442}}.
